short_description: Enveloped flavivirus (genus Orthoflavivirus, ~40-65 nm, roughly 50 nm) with a +ssRNA genome (~10.7 kb) wrapped by a relatively unstructured capsid (C) protein shell, surrounded by a host-derived lipid envelope. The defining feature is the outer surface: 180 copies of the envelope (E) glycoprotein sit as 90 head-to-tail dimers lying FLAT against the membrane in an icosahedral herringbone raft, giving a smooth, tiled, spike-free surface - a golf-ball or woven-basket texture, never a corona of projecting spikes. Spread by day-biting Aedes mosquitoes; usually mild or unnoticed, but crosses the placenta and can disturb fetal brain development.

colour_legend.genome: warm amber/gold, loosely coiled +ssRNA thread filling the core - a soft tangled ball, NOT a tidy double helix (that would be DNA)
colour_legend.capsid: pale warm grey-tan, a soft, slightly irregular inner shell of C protein hugging the genome - deliberately less crisply faceted/geometric than a bacteriophage or herpesvirus capsid, since the flavivirus C-protein shell is comparatively disordered
colour_legend.envelope: translucent cool grey-lilac lipid bilayer just beneath the surface tiling, host-derived and reasonably smooth/round
colour_legend.e_glycoprotein_tiling: dusty rose/mauve flat interlocking dimers tiled edge-to-edge over the whole outer surface in a herringbone/basket-weave pattern - like the seams of a football or the dimples of a golf ball - completely SMOOTH in silhouette, no studs, no bumps, no projections
colour_legend.m_protein: a thin cool blue-grey undercoat glimpsed only in tiny gaps of the tiling or in the cutaway, tucked directly beneath the E layer against the envelope
colour_legend.background: neutral dark charcoal (watercolour: warm aged paper)
colour_legend.note: A virion has no pigment of its own; real cryo-EM/TEM reference images this in greyscale, so colour is teaching convention. Keep this structure->colour mapping across sem/textbook/3d/watercolor. The single most important visual idea to get across is SMOOTHNESS: the tiled E-protein raft reads as texture (facets/seams), never as anything protruding.

do_not_draw: ANY protruding spikes of any kind - no coronavirus-style club-shaped spikes, no influenza-style HA/NA projections, no rod-like or knob-like studs sticking out of the surface. This is the single most important error to avoid: Zika's E glycoproteins lie FLAT against the membrane, they do not project outward.

a bald, featureless, perfectly smooth sphere with no surface texture at all - the E-protein herringbone tiling should read as a subtle woven/faceted/dimpled texture (like a golf ball or a woven rattan ball), not literally blank
a naked capsid with no envelope - Zika is ALWAYS enveloped, unlike the non-enveloped rotavirus/norovirus already in this atlas

a tegument layer or any granular padding between capsid and envelope - that is a herpesvirus feature (varicella-zoster virus in this atlas); Zika's capsid sits directly under the envelope with no such layer
a helical, rod-shaped or filamentous capsid, or a bacteriophage head-and-tail body with tail fibres/base plate
a segmented genome, or a double-stranded / helical DNA molecule - the genome is a single molecule of positive-sense single-stranded RNA, not DNA, not segmented
bacterial features: cell wall, peptidoglycan, flagellum, pilus, capsule, nucleoid, ribosomes, mitochondria or any cell organelle - a virion is not a cell

a mosquito, a mosquito bite, a pregnant belly, a fetus, or any depiction of microcephaly/birth defects in the four science styles (sem/textbook/3d/watercolor) - those are transmission/clinical context, not virus morphology, and (per the brief) the pregnancy risk must not appear at all in the kids' materials and should be handled plainly, without alarm, only in the adult/scientific text blocks
a face, eyes, mouth or anthropomorphism on the virion in the four science styles (reserved for the separate kids' coloring page only)
any baked-in text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars, rulers, legends or watermarks
a black border, dark frame, vignette, letterbox bar, mat, drop shadow, or the artwork drawn as a sheet/card lying on a surface

sources.claim: Zika virus is a member of genus Orthoflavivirus (Flaviviridae), ~40-65 nm (commonly cited as ~40-50 nm), enveloped, icosahedral; +ssRNA genome of ~10.7 kb with a single open reading frame encoding 3 structural proteins (C, prM/M, E) and 7 nonstructural proteins (NS1, NS2A, NS2B, NS3, NS4A, NS4B, NS5)
sources.source: Standard flavivirus virology consistent with ICTV Flaviviridae taxonomy and CDC/WHO Zika fact sheets; cross-checked against the closely related, structurally near-identical dengue virus for which high-resolution cryo-EM structures are published (Kostyuchenko et al. 2016, Nature, 'Structure of the thermally stable Zika virus'; Sirohi et al. 2016, Science, 'The 3.8 A resolution cryo-EM structure of Zika virus').

sources.claim: the mature flavivirus surface is smooth: 180 copies of the E glycoprotein pack as 90 head-to-tail homodimers lying flat/parallel to the lipid envelope in an icosahedral herringbone arrangement (T=1 pseudo-T=3 lattice), giving a continuous, spike-free, geometrically faceted-but-smooth shell (unlike alphaviruses, which display projecting E-protein spikes); the M protein is a small protein retained under the E layer after furin cleavage of prM during maturation; the capsid (C) protein forms a comparatively disordered nucleocapsid core around the genome rather than a rigid icosahedral shell
sources.source: Sirohi D. et al. 2016, Science 352(6284):467-470, 'The 3.8 A resolution cryo-EM structure of Zika virus' (describes the smooth herringbone E-dimer raft characteristic of flaviviruses, near-identical to dengue); consistent with general flavivirus structural biology reviews.

sources.claim: transmitted primarily by day-biting Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes; also by sexual contact and vertically (transplacental) from mother to fetus; most infections are mild or asymptomatic (low-grade fever, maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, arthralgia); the principal serious risk is congenital Zika syndrome (microcephaly and other brain abnormalities) following infection during pregnancy, and a smaller elevated risk of Guillain-Barre syndrome in adults; no licensed vaccine as of 2026
sources.source: CDC Zika virus fact sheets and WHO Zika virus disease fact sheet, consistent with the func_en/deps_en text already in this project's cells_data.py.

reference.license: Public domain - CDC Public Health Image Library states 'None - This image is in the public domain and thus free of any copyright restrictions.'
reference.modality: digitally colorized transmission electron microscopy (TEM), false-colour (virions red, tissue purple)
reference.native_pixel_size: 700 x 700 px JPEG (151,982 bytes), verified via curl -sIL (HTTP 200, image/jpeg) and Pillow
reference.verified: curl -sIL returned HTTP 200 (phil.cdc.gov redirects to wwwn.cdc.gov); content-type image/jpeg, 151982 bytes; dimensions 700x700 confirmed with Pillow. Visually verified by direct inspection: ~15 round, ~40 nm false-colour-red virions scattered through purple-stained tissue, no baked-in text, arrow or scale bar. A companion plate at the same field of view, PHIL ID 20487 (greyscale, uncolourized), carries a baked-in arrow pointing at one particle and was therefore rejected as the base image; 20538 is the arrow-free colourized twin of the same field.
reference.note: Group shot, not a single isolated particle - the best available public-domain Zika micrograph at conventional TEM resolution shows several ~40-50 nm virions in stained brain tissue rather than one isolated specimen; individual particles are clearly readable as small round dots with a discernible denser rim, but the herringbone surface texture is below this plate's resolution (not expected to be visible at this magnification/staining). Accepted per the pipeline's 'group acceptable if the microbe's features are clearly readable' guidance - shape, rough size and count are unambiguous even though fine surface texture is not resolvable. fetch_reference.py uses the native 700x700 image and upscales (Lanczos) to the standard 1080x1080 canvas - an explicit upscale from native resolution, not additional real detail. No baked-in text or scale bar was present, so edit_image.py was intentionally skipped.
